examples.en: Grandma pampers and looks after him all the time.

note: Said when one person looks after another with special attention.

examples.sr: То је само [ре̏кла-ка̏за̄ла̄], немој да верујеш.
examples.en: That's just hearsay, don't believe it.

note: From «баба је рекла-казала»: unverified information, third-hand.

examples.en: These jeans are the real thing: they can take any amount of wear.

note: Said of clothes that can take any rough use.

meanings: pencil or pen with an eraser

examples.en: I have a pencil with an eraser in my bag.

note: A jokey name for a writing tool that can also erase.

examples.en: There's stop-and-go traffic on the bridge again.

note: Said of heavy traffic on the roads.

meanings: there's no such thing as a free lunch
forms: literally: there is no free bread

examples.en: There's no such thing as a free lunch, you'll have to work.

note: Said to someone who wants something without paying for it. «џабе» means «for free».

meanings: don't count your chickens before they hatch
forms: literally: bake it, then say it

examples.en: Wait, don't count your chickens before they hatch!

note: Don't boast until the job is done.

examples.sr: На слави је било довољно [и́ће и пи́ће].
examples.en: There was enough food and drink at the slava.

note: A rhyming expression: «иће» is food, «пиће» is a drink.

examples.sr: Ове године идемо [на мо̑ре] у Грчку.
examples.en: This year we're going to the seaside in Greece.

note: Going: «на» + acc.; being there: «на» + loc. («бити на мору»). Also «ићи на одмор» - to go on vacation.

examples.en: I can't hear you, the connection is acting up.

note: A playful rhyme from a song of the series «Радио Милева»: «зезати» is to tease or let down; of equipment, to act up.

examples.sr: [Ка̀ко се зо̏ве о̀на ства̑р] за кување кафе?
examples.en: What's that thing called that you make coffee with?

note: A way around a forgotten word: «она ствар, коју користимо за...». For an appliance say «онај уређај»; for something nearby, «ова ствар».

examples.en: Put on a longer shirt, keep your lower back covered!

note: Concern for the lower back and kidneys: Serbs believe a bare back is dangerous. Related: «затвори прозор, промаја је!» (close the window, there's a draft) and «упаши се!» (tuck your shirt in).

examples.en: Close the window, there's a draft!

note: Fear of drafts is almost a national trait: it is why windows get shut in transport and at home.

examples.sr: Извини, [у гу̑жвӣ сам], јавићу ти се касније.
examples.en: Sorry, I'm swamped, I'll get back to you later.

note: A universal excuse for not being able to help or talk. For being late, just say «гужва је» (traffic, crowds).

meanings: repetition is the mother of learning
forms: literally: repetition is the mother of knowledge

examples.sr: [Пона́вља̄ње је ма̏јка зна̏ња], зато учимо сваки дан.
examples.en: Repetition is the mother of learning, so we study every day.

note: A school proverb, one of the best known among Serbs.

examples.en: Happy March 8th!
Happy New Year!

note: A universal greeting: «срећан» + the holiday, with the ending matching its gender: срећан Ускрс, срећна Нова година. A country is greeted the same way: «Србијо, срећан Дан државности!».

examples.en: Hats off for such effort!

examples.sr: Кад видим како ради, кажем: [ка̏па до̏ле].
examples.en: When I see how he works, I say: hats off.

note: Respect for someone's deed or success; as in the song about Novak: «Ноле, капа доле».

meanings: not for anything in the world
forms: literally: not for a living head

examples.sr: Тамо не идем [ни за жѝву гла̑ву].
examples.en: I'm not going there for anything in the world.

examples.sr: [Ни за жѝву гла̑ву] га не бих издала.
examples.en: I wouldn't betray him for anything in the world.

note: A set expression for a flat refusal.

examples.en: His smile was a kiss of Judas.
- Anything else? - That's all, thanks.
I found the medicine. That's the one!

note: Meaning depends on the situation: at the checkout, «that's all»; on finding what you looked for, «that's the one»; at the end, «that's it»; after a fix, «now it's right»; on a guess, «you got it»; «it's a deal».

examples.sr: Није много, али [бо̏ље̄ и̏шта не̏го ни̏шта].
examples.en: It's not much, but it's better than nothing.

examples.sr: - [Шта̏ и̏ма] ново? - Ништа, све по старом.
examples.en: - What's new? - Nothing, same as ever.
What's up, buddy?

note: A greeting between acquaintances; the usual answer is «Ништа» - nothing special.

examples.en: Don't worry, it's no big deal.

examples.sr: - Извини што сам закаснио. - [Нѝје то̑ ни̏шта].
examples.en: - Sorry I'm late. - No problem.

note: Used to reassure someone or to accept an apology.

examples.sr: Пао је с бицикла, али [нѝје му ни̏шта].
examples.en: He fell off his bike, but he's fine.
Don't worry, she's fine.

note: About health: the person is not ill or hurt.

examples.en: I hurt myself badly on the slippery floor.
Don't run, you'll hurt yourself!

note: Literally «to kill oneself», but it means a hard knock or bruise. «убити» is common in everyday talk: «убија ме промаја» - a draft is really bothering me.

examples.sr: Кад је испричао виц, [цр̏као сам од сме̏ха].
examples.en: When he told the joke, I died laughing.

examples.sr: [Цр̏кла сам од сме̏ха] на његовој причи.
examples.en: I cracked up at his story.

note: «цркнути» (to croak) is rather coarse. More neutral: «умирем од смеха».

examples.en: He was dead serious when he said it.
I'm not joking, I'm dead serious.

note: Similar intensifiers: «мртав пијан» - dead drunk, «мртав хладан» - cool as ice.

examples.sr: Сви су вриштали, а он [мр̀тав хла́дан].
examples.en: Everyone was screaming, and he didn't turn a hair.

note: A person whose face shows no emotion at all.

forms: literally: does a dead man want earth?

examples.en: - Do you want coffee? - You bet!

note: A jokey rhetorical question in reply to «do you want...?» when the answer is obvious.

examples.en: Take care of yourself.
Make sure you don't miss the bus.

note: A parting wish, or just a request to be careful. «о» + loc.: «о себи».

forms: literally: it went for me along the hand

examples.sr: [По̏шло ми је за ру́ко̄м] да добијем визу.
examples.en: I managed to get a visa.

examples.sr: Коначно му је [по̏шло за ру́ко̄м] да положи испит.
examples.en: He finally managed to pass the exam.

note: Said of a success reached after effort.

forms: literally: it has stood to me up to

examples.sr: Много ми је [ста̏ло] до тог посла.
examples.en: That job matters a lot to me.

examples.sr: Знаш да ми је [ста̏ло] до тебе.
examples.en: You know I care about you.

note: Construction: «стало ми је до» + gen.

examples.en: I don't want to see you, get lost!

note: Rude, only in a quarrel.

examples.en: She dressed up for the wedding.

examples.sr: Увек се [ско̏цка] кад иде у град.
examples.en: She always dresses up when she goes into town.

note: A colloquial word; in compliments also «сређена» (well put together) and «дотерана» (nicely dressed).

examples.en: It's clearing up outside, we can go for a walk.
Cloudy in the morning, clearing up later.

note: About the weather; the opposite is «облачи се» (it's clouding over).

examples.en: Excuse me, could we have the check?
The check, please.

note: The same pattern «Може» + what you ask for works for the menu: «Може јеловник?».

examples.sr: - Да ли сте спремни? - Не, [јо̏ш би̏рамо].
examples.en: - Are you ready? - No, we're still choosing.

note: A reply to the waiter; when ready to order: «Спремни смо да поручимо».

examples.en: Keep it, keep the change.
Keep the change, thanks.

note: Can also be said briefly: «У реду је».

meanings: I'd like to reserve a table

examples.sr: [Хте̏ла бих да резѐрвишем сто̑] за вечерас.
examples.en: I'd like to reserve a table for tonight.

examples.sr: [Хте̏о бих да резѐрвишем сто̑] за четворо у осам.
examples.en: I'd like to reserve a table for four at eight.

note: A woman says «хтела бих».

meanings: what will you have to drink?

examples.en: Good evening, what will you have to drink?

note: A waiter's question; «од» + gen. means 'out of'.

examples.en: I feel sick, I need some air.
I feel better after the medicine.

note: Similar: «Није ми добро» - I'm not feeling well, «Погоршало ми је» - I got worse.

forms: literally: your car is the top

examples.en: Your car is just awesome!

note: Colloquial «врх» means the best, top class; it can be said of anything: «Овај филм је врх».

examples.sr: Није видео знак, али [Бо̑г чу̏ва бу̀дале].
examples.en: He didn't see the sign, but God looks after fools.

note: Said when someone narrowly avoided trouble through carelessness, often jokingly about oneself.

examples.en: You cheeky thing, you ate everything!

note: «Што» is exclamatory here: 'how'. A playful reproach, like «Баш си сладак!» (ironic: aren't you sweet).

examples.en: Make a wish and blow out the candle.
I want to make your wish come true.

note: «жеља» is a wish or desire; not to be confused with «сан» (a dream, an aspiration).

examples.en: Happy March 8th, dear ladies!

note: In Serbia the day is marked with flowers and a box of chocolates; it is a working day.

examples.en: For God's sake, what are you saying?

note: Often with «бре»: Човече божји, бре! Expresses outrage or amazement.

meanings: where have you been? (glad to see you)

examples.sr: [Где̏ си, бре̏]? Сто година те нисам видео!
examples.en: Where have you been? I haven't seen you in ages!

examples.sr: [Где̏ си, бре̏]? Чекамо те сат времена!
examples.en: Where are you? We've been waiting for you for an hour!

note: Intonation sets the meaning; «бре» adds emotion.

forms: literally: to pay with the head

examples.en: He paid for the mistake with his life.

note: A serious expression, about grave consequences.

examples.en: - When will you get a job? - Any day now!

note: A joking dodge to nosy questions about a wedding, children, a degree: «Кад ће крај факултета?» (when will you finish college?).

key: phr:сви ће мислити да си рус
meanings: everyone will think you're Russian (a joke to someone underdressed for the cold)
forms: literally: everyone will think you're a Russian

examples.sr: Без јакне по хладном? [Сви̏ ће ми̏слити да си Ру̏с]!
examples.en: No jacket in this cold? Everyone will think you're Russian!

note: Serbs joke that Russians don't feel the cold.

meanings: I've got my period (a blunt euphemism among Serbian women)

examples.en: I can't swim, I've got my period.
My stomach hurts, I got my period.

note: Serbs talk about it openly, even around men. Only the feminine form is used: it is a remark for women.

examples.en: - How much? - I'm joking, April Fools!

note: How Serbs announce that they were joking. April 1 is «Дан првоаприлске шале»; it is marked with pranks, not as a holiday.

meanings: what's with you? (a reproach for odd behavior)
forms: literally: what kind of style is this of yours

examples.sr: [Ка̀ка̄в ти је то̑ фа̏зон]? Обећаш па не дођеш!
examples.en: What's with you? You promise and then you don't show up!

note: A colloquial reproach. «Он је у свом фазону» - he's being his usual self.

meanings: how do you say it in Italian?
forms: literally: how is it said in Italian

examples.en: How do you say 'thank you' in Italian?

note: To ask for a translation: «како се каже» + «на» + the language in the locative.

forms: literally: what is it being done about

examples.sr: [О чѐму се ра̏ди]? Зашто сви вичу?
examples.en: What's going on? Why is everyone shouting?

note: «Радити се о» means 'to be about, to be a matter of'.

examples.en: We're going out tonight, where shall we go?

note: A question about future plans: Serbian says «где» (where) also for 'where to'.

forms: literally: how do you think that

examples.en: - I won't come. - How so?

note: A polite or surprised request for clarification.

meanings: would you like something to drink?
forms: literally: are you for a drink

examples.sr: [Да ли сте за пи́ће]? Имамо чај и сок.
examples.en: Would you like something to drink? We have tea and juice.

note: How a host offers drinks. Similar: «Јеси ли за кафу?» (do you fancy a coffee?).

meanings: a stock greeting: busy, are you?

examples.sr: - [Јѐси ли вре́дан]? - Јесам, радим цео дан.
examples.en: - Hard at work? - Yes, I work all day.

note: Not a question about character, but a casual greeting to someone who is busy.

forms: literally: it's not all the same to me

examples.en: When I drive at night, I feel uneasy.

examples.sr: [Нѝје ми би̏ло свејѐдно] на том путу.
examples.en: I was scared on that road.

note: Not «I don't mind» but «I'm uneasy».

examples.en: Good morning, how did you sleep?
Morning! The coffee is ready.

note: The short «Јутро!» is for friends and family.

meanings: what luck (said of a first child who is a boy)
forms: literally: first, and a boy at that

examples.en: They had a son: first and a boy!

note: A traditional congratulation to the father. For a girl they say «Само нек је живо и здраво!» (as long as the baby is alive and well).

meanings: to take on a hopeless task
forms: literally: to straighten the crooked Drinas

examples.sr: Не губи време, то је као [ѝсправљати кри̏ве Дри̏не].
examples.en: Don't waste your time, it's like trying to straighten the crooked Drina.

note: The river Drina winds and cannot be straightened. Said of futile effort.

examples.sr: Ове године је мој син [ђа̑к пр̀ва̄к].
examples.en: My son is a first grader this year.

note: First graders have a special status: they get no grades, only descriptive comments.

forms: literally: if it passes, it passes

examples.en: I didn't prepare anything, so let's hope for the best.

note: Serbs often rely on luck.

examples.en: He got the job through connections.

note: Like «преко реда» - out of turn, ahead of the queue.

meanings: that's just how it is (with a shrug)

examples.en: - Why? - That's just how it is!
We didn't win, oh well.

note: Serbs don't regard it as real profanity. It expresses resignation and helplessness. A foreigner should use it with care.

meanings: to be embarrassed to speak Serbian
forms: literally: I'm ashamed to speak Serbian

examples.sr: Она се [сти̏ди да при̑ча] са странцима.
examples.en: She's embarrassed to talk to foreigners.
I'm not embarrassed to speak Serbian.

note: For languages, «говорити» is better: говорити српски, руски, енглески. «Причати» means to chat or tell.

forms: literally: it really did me good

examples.sr: Хвала на ручку, [ба̏ш ми је при̏јало]!
examples.en: Thanks for lunch, it really hit the spot!
The vacation did me a lot of good.

note: The hostess answers: «Баш ми је драго!» (I'm really glad).

examples.en: All citizens must obey the law.

examples.sr: Молимо вас да [др̏жите расто̀јање] од једног метра.
examples.en: Please keep a distance of one meter.

note: The same verb «држати» is in «држати дијету» - to be on a diet.

forms: literally: to get at the lottery

examples.sr: Комшија је [до̀био на лу̀трији] нови аутомобил.
examples.en: The neighbor won a new car in the lottery.

note: To win a prize is «добити» (to get), not «победити»; the lottery takes «на» + loc.

examples.sr: Време је да се [опасу̀љиш] и почнеш да учиш.
examples.en: It's time to come to your senses and start studying.

note: Humorous, formed from «пасуљ» (beans). Said to someone behaving recklessly.

examples.sr: У дизајну важи правило: [ма̏ње је ви̏ше].
examples.en: In design the rule is: less is more.
Everyone is more or less satisfied.
I roughly know how much it costs.

note: Not to be confused with «мање је више»: this is an adverb of approximation, not a proverb.

examples.en: I didn't get the award, April Fools!

note: Shouted after pranking someone on April 1. The day of jokes is «дан шале». A favorite character of Serbian jokes is the boy Перица.

examples.en: Open the window, it's smoky in here.

note: Also «задимљено је» and «загушљиво је» (stuffy). Not to be confused with «напушен» - slang for 'stoned'.

meanings: hot dishes of the day (on a café sign)

examples.sr: Овде имају добра [ку̏вана је̏ла] сваког дана.
examples.en: They have good home-cooked meals here every day.

note: Not necessarily boiled: the menu may include fried or breaded dishes too. As opposed to fast food, pastries and sandwiches.

meanings: spoon dishes: soups and stews (chorba, beans, goulash)

examples.en: For lunch I like something you eat with a spoon.

note: Serbs automatically associate home cooking with good quality and healthy food.

examples.en: The exam is tomorrow, I'm rooting for you!

note: To root for someone is «навијати за» + acc. Not «болети» (to hurt).

examples.en: Step aside, please, I'm coming through.

note: More polite: «помери се» (move over); rude: «макни се». To sound warmer, add an address: «бато» (bro), «секо» (sis).

meanings: in the middle of the night

examples.sr: Позвао ме је [у глу̏во до̑ба] ноћи.
examples.en: He called me in the dead of night.
Why are you awake in the middle of the night?

note: Often «у глуво доба ноћи»; the darkest and quietest time of night.

meanings: whoever survives will tell the tale (joking, of a hectic period)

examples.sr: Седам рођендана за недељу дана - [ко̏ прѐживи, при̏чаће]!
examples.en: Seven birthdays in one week - whoever survives will tell the tale!

note: A joking saying before something hard or chaotic; said with irony.

meanings: at the top of one's voice

examples.en: The children are singing at the top of their voices.

examples.sr: Викао је [на са̏в гла̑с] да га сви чују.
examples.en: He shouted at the top of his voice so everyone could hear.

note: Used with verbs of singing, shouting, laughing.

meanings: completely innocent (of a conscience, a window)

examples.en: My conscience is perfectly clear.
The window was spotless.

note: For Serbs a tear is an image of utmost purity; the comparison is also used jokingly.

examples.en: The sign on the fence says: danger of death.

note: The wording on warning signs; «по» + acc.

meanings: it isn't hard to be nice
forms: literally: it's not hard to be nice

examples.sr: Само се насмеши, [нѝје те̑шко би̏ти фи̑н].
examples.en: Just smile, it isn't hard to be nice.

examples.sr: Рекла сам му да [нѝје те̑шко би̏ти фи̑н] према људима.
examples.en: I told him it isn't hard to be nice to people.

note: A mild reproach to someone rude; «фин» here means polite, pleasant to deal with.

examples.en: You're on vacation? Lucky you!
Lucky you, being at home.

note: Said with joy or a bit of envy at someone's luck; other persons: «благо мени», «благо њему», «благо вама».

examples.en: We bought shoes at the department store.

note: Here «кућа» is a business; similar: «модна кућа» (fashion house), «издавачка кућа» (publishing house).

examples.en: I have to go to the clinic for a certificate.
The clinic is open until seven in the evening.

note: A public institution for primary care and doctor visits, not a residence.

examples.sr: На граници је била права [лу̏да ку̏ћа].
examples.en: It was a real madhouse at the border.

note: The figurative meaning is used for noisy disorder.

examples.en: Put that down, it's dangerous!
Jovan, put that down right now!

note: How parents tell off children; also heard: «Стани!» (stop) and «Не!» (no).

forms: literally: at what price are the strawberries

examples.en: How much are the strawberries, please?
How much do these berries cost?

note: Serbs usually say «јагоде» in the plural, as on price tags; «пошто» is the colloquial 'how much'.

forms: literally: you are lacking to me

examples.en: I've been missing you for days.
I don't have enough time for my family.

note: The subject is the person missed: «недостајеш ми» is literally 'you are lacking to me'; for a lack of a thing, «недостаје ми».

examples.en: What are you talking about, that's not true!
Don't talk nonsense, please.

note: A colloquial reply to boasting or nonsense; a bit rude, but friendly between pals.

examples.en: It's forty degrees Celsius outside, I'm boiling.
We were boiling on the bus.

note: About intense heat; a man says «скувао сам се». A similar phrase for tiredness: «цркла сам».

examples.en: After the move I'm wiped out.
I'm worn out from work.

note: Colloquial and vivid; a man says «цркао сам». Heard often; in polite speech use «исцрпљена сам».

key: phr:није коме је намењено, већ коме је суђено
meanings: it goes not to the one it was meant for, but to the one it's destined for
forms: literally: not to whom it is intended, but to whom it is fated

examples.sr: Посао је добио други: [нѝје ко̀ме је на̀мењено, ве̏ћ ко̀ме је су̏ђено].
examples.en: Someone else got the job: it goes not to the one it was meant for, but to the one it's destined for.

note: A proverb about fate; said philosophically, consoling oneself or someone else after a setback.

meanings: I offered, so I've done my part

examples.en: You're not eating? Fine, I offered, so I've done my part.

note: Said when a guest turns down food: the host has done his part.

key: phr:ко се с нама дружи, живот му је дуже
meanings: whoever hangs out with us lives longer (a table toast)
forms: literally: whoever keeps company with us, his life is longer

examples.sr: [Ко̏ се с на̏ма дру̏жи], никад му није досадно.
examples.en: Whoever hangs out with us is never bored.

note: A jokey toast at the table; it continues: «ко са нама пије, досадно му није» (whoever drinks with us is never bored).

meanings: pint-sized (a short person, jokingly or sarcastically)
forms: literally: a meter and a wish to grow

examples.sr: Онај дечак је [ме̏тар и же̏ља да по̀расте].
examples.en: That kid is knee-high to a grasshopper.

note: An ironic way of describing short height.

examples.en: She got an engagement ring for her birthday.
The wedding band is plain, with no stone.

note: Not to be confused with «бурма» - the wedding band worn at the wedding.

forms: literally: to be in the element

examples.en: I'm in my element today.

examples.sr: Није [у елѐменту], боље га не дирај.
examples.en: He's out of sorts, better leave him alone.

note: Negated, «нисам у елементу» means off form, low on energy; also used to explain teenage moods.

key: phr:чувати беле паре за црне дане
meanings: to save for a rainy day
forms: literally: to keep white money for black days

examples.sr: Увек [чу̏ва бѐле па̑ре за цр̀не да̑не].
examples.en: He always saves for a rainy day.

note: «беле паре» are silver coins, i.e. real savings; «црни дани» are hard times.

key: phr:шта ће ми те црне паре
meanings: what good is this damn money? (annoyance)
forms: literally: what do I need this black money for

examples.sr: [Шта̏ ће ми те цр̀не па̑ре] ако немам времена?
examples.en: What good is this damn money if I have no time?

note: «црн» here intensifies the irritation; it is not a color.

examples.en: Sometimes we go fishing.
Oh, my boy, what have you done?

note: The meaning depends on the intonation: you can pity or reproach.

meanings: what ... are you talking about! (a sarcastic objection)

examples.sr: [Ка̀ка̄в цр̑нӣ о̀дмор]! Радио сам све време.
examples.en: What vacation! I worked the whole time.

note: «црн» strengthens the denial: the speaker disagrees with the very word.

examples.en: How much is a kilo of apples?

note: A colloquial variant of «Колико кошта?». Answer: «Сто динара кило» (a hundred dinars a kilo).

meanings: can you make it cheaper? (asking for a discount)

examples.en: Can you do it cheaper? I'm buying five.
It's nice, but it's too expensive for me.

note: The person for whom it is expensive goes in the dative: ми, ти, му.

forms: literally: a kilogram and a half

examples.en: Give me a kilo and a half of potatoes.

note: The same pattern: сат и по (an hour and a half), метар и по. Half a kilo is «полкило».

examples.en: The check, please. I'll pay in cash.

note: To pay by card: «картицом»; in cash: «готовином».

examples.sr: [Нѝје та̏чно], он је стигао у пет.
examples.en: That's not right, he arrived at five.

note: Often sounds like a polite «no, you're mistaken».

examples.en: I prefer the theater to the movies.

note: To compare, use «него»: више волим чај него кафу.

examples.en: The sign on the gate says: Beware of the dog!

note: «чувати се» + gen. means to beware of something.

examples.en: Don't touch that, it's hot!

note: On door signs: «Вуци» - pull, «Гурај» - push.

meanings: I wish you all the best

examples.en: I wish you all the best in your new life.

key: phr:кад мачке нема, мишеви коло воде
meanings: when the cat's away, the mice will play
forms: literally: when there is no cat, the mice lead the kolo

examples.sr: Шеф је отишао, [ка̏д ма̏чке нѐма, мѝшеви ко̏ло во̀де].
examples.en: The boss has left: when the cat's away, the mice will play.

note: «коло» is a folk circle dance.

forms: literally: there is no smoke without fire

examples.sr: Људи причају, а [нѐма ди̏ма без ва̏тре].
examples.en: People are talking, and there's no smoke without fire.

meanings: to make a mountain out of a molehill
forms: literally: to make a donkey out of a mosquito

examples.en: Don't make a mountain out of a molehill.

note: Serbian has a mosquito and a donkey where English has a molehill and a mountain.

key: phr:што можеш данас, не остављај за сутра
meanings: never put off till tomorrow what you can do today
forms: literally: what you can do today, don't leave for tomorrow

examples.sr: Заврши посао: [што̏ мо̏жеш да̀нас, не оста̀вљај за су̏тра].
examples.en: Finish the work: never put off till tomorrow what you can do today.

key: phr:ивер не пада далеко од кладе
meanings: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree
forms: literally: a splinter doesn't fall far from the log

examples.sr: Отац и син су исти: [и̏ве̄р не па̏да далѐко од кла̀де].
examples.en: Father and son are just alike: the apple doesn't fall far from the tree.

key: phr:ако будеш мост, свако ће да те гази
meanings: if you let people use you, they will walk all over you
forms: literally: if you are a bridge, everyone will trample you

examples.sr: Кажем ти: [а̏ко бу̏де̄ш мо̑ст, сва̑ко ће да те га̀зи].
examples.en: I'm telling you: if you're a bridge, everyone will walk all over you.

key: phr:ако слепац слепца води, обојица ће у јаму упасти
forms: literally: if a blind man leads a blind man, both will fall into a pit

examples.sr: Он не зна ништа, а учи другог: [а̏ко сле́пац сле̏пца во̀ди, обо̀јица ће у ја̑му у̀пасти].
examples.en: He knows nothing himself, yet he teaches others: the blind leading the blind.

key: phr:боља је своја проја него туђа погача
meanings: better your own humble bread than someone else's fancy loaf
forms: literally: better your own proja than a stranger's pogača

examples.sr: Радије сам код куће: [бо̀ља је сво̀ја про̏ја не̏го ту̑ђа пога̀ча].
examples.en: I'd rather be at home: better your own humble bread than someone else's fancy loaf.

note: «проја» is cornbread, «погача» a festive wheat bread.

key: phr:боље из далека се волети него изблиза мрзети
meanings: better to love from afar than to hate up close
forms: literally: better to love from afar than to hate from close by

examples.sr: Не селимо заједно: [бо̏ље̄ из далѐка се во̀лети не̏го и̏зблӣза мр́зети].
examples.en: We're not moving in together: better to love each other from afar than to hate each other up close.

key: phr:може ли да се плати картицом
forms: literally: can one pay by card

examples.sr: [Мо̏же ли да се пла̏ти ка̏ртицом]? - Да, може.
examples.en: Can I pay by card? - Yes, you can.

note: A shop's answer: «Само готовином» - cash only.

examples.en: Excuse me, where's my change?

forms: literally: don't use the formal «you» with me

examples.sr: [Нѐмој да ми персѝраш], ја сам Марко.
examples.en: Don't be so formal with me, I'm Marko.

note: Serbs switch to «ти» (informal you) quickly: sellers and waiters may also say «ти» to you.

examples.en: - Are you coming to dinner? - Of course!

examples.sr: [За̑р то̑ мо̏же бѝти]? Јуче је још било лето.
examples.en: Can that really be? Yesterday it was still summer.

note: «Зар» is a particle of disbelief: «Зар не знаш?» - Don't you know?

examples.en: We won! Just imagine!

note: To several people or politely: «Само замислите!».

forms: literally: a shiver passes through me

examples.sr: Кад чујем ту песму, [про̀лази ме је́за].
examples.en: When I hear that song, I get shivers.

note: From illness and from strong feelings alike.

examples.en: I'm not coming to work, I have a cold.
Excuse me, I'm in a hurry, I have a train to catch.

note: An impersonal construction, like «спава ми се»: the person in a hurry or wanting to sleep goes in the dative.

examples.en: Wait a moment, I'll be right back.
Sorry, I have no small change.

note: «Ситно» is small money; «ситнина» is coins.

key: phr:у реду је, остатак је за вас
forms: literally: it's in order, the rest is for you

examples.sr: [У ре̑ду је, оста́так је за вас].
examples.en: It's fine, keep the change.

note: Said to a taxi driver or waiter when leaving a tip.

forms: literally: I have no more gasoline

examples.en: We've stopped: I'm out of gas.
There was an accident on the road.
Your driver's license, please.

note: The vehicle registration is «саобраћајна дозвола».

forms: literally: like Christmas Eve and Christmas

examples.sr: Њих двојица су [ка̏о Ба̑дњи да̑н и Бо̀жић].
examples.en: Those two are inseparable.

note: Christmas Eve and Christmas follow one right after the other.

key: phr:да ти свака жеља постане стварност
meanings: may all your wishes come true
forms: literally: may your every wish become reality

examples.sr: За рођендан ти желим: [да ти сва̏ка̄ же̏ља по̀стане̄ ства́рно̄ст].
examples.en: For your birthday I wish you this: may all your wishes come true.

key: phr:желим вам пуно здравља и среће
meanings: I wish you good health and happiness
forms: literally: I wish you much health and happiness

examples.sr: [Же̏лим вам пу̏но здра̑вља и сре̑ће] у Новој години.
examples.en: I wish you good health and happiness in the New Year.

note: After «желим» use the genitive: здравља, среће, успеха.

forms: literally: how much does this cost

examples.en: Excuse me, how much does this cost?

note: Answer: «Ово кошта педесет динара.» / «Цена је ...».

examples.sr: [Мо̀гу ли о̀во̄ да про̏бам]? Где је кабина?
examples.en: Can I try this on? Where is the fitting room?

note: «Пробати» means both to taste and to try on; the fitting room is «кабина за пробу».

key: phr:имате ли ово у другој боји
meanings: do you have this in another color (size)?
forms: literally: do you have this in another color

examples.en: Do you have this in another color?

note: Instead of «боји» you can say «величини» - size.

forms: literally: you have exceeded the speed

examples.en: Sir, you were speeding.

note: A fine is «казна»: «Мораћете да платите казну» (you will have to pay a fine).

examples.sr: Дошао си касно, али [бо̏ље̄ и̏кад не̏го ни̏кад].
examples.en: You came late, but better late than never.

meanings: better to bend than to break
forms: literally: better to bend than to break

examples.en: Give a little: better to bend than to break.

key: phr:боље се оградити добрим комшијом него добром оградом
meanings: a good neighbor is better than any fence
forms: literally: better to fence yourself in with a good neighbor than with a good fence

examples.sr: Имам добре комшије: [бо̏ље̄ се огра́дити до̀брим ко̀мшијом не̏го до̀бром огра̀дом].
examples.en: I have good neighbors: a good neighbor is better than any fence.

forms: literally: every stick has two ends

examples.en: Careful, it cuts both ways.

meanings: everyone is the maker of their own fortune
forms: literally: everyone is the smith of their own luck

examples.sr: Не чекај помоћ: [сва̑ко је сво̀је сре̑ће ко̀ва̄ч].
examples.en: Don't wait for help: everyone is the maker of their own fortune.
Don't give up, every beginning is hard.

meanings: you're never too old to learn
forms: literally: a person learns until death

examples.sr: Ни ја не знам све: [чо̀век се до смр̑ти у̏чи].
examples.en: I don't know everything either: you live and learn.

examples.sr: Не хвали се: [до̏бар по̀сао се сам хва̏ли].
examples.en: Don't brag: good work speaks for itself.

meanings: birds of a feather flock together
forms: literally: every bird flies to its own flock

examples.sr: Увек се друже заједно: [сва̏ка̄ пти̑ца сво̑ме ја̑ту лѐти].
examples.en: They're always together: birds of a feather flock together.

key: phr:свак по себи суди о другоме
forms: literally: everyone judges another by himself

examples.sr: Не љути се: [сва̑к по се̏би су̏ди о дру̀гоме].
examples.en: Don't be offended: people judge others by themselves.

key: phr:човек без слободе као риба без воде
meanings: a man without freedom is like a fish out of water
forms: literally: a man without freedom, like a fish without water

examples.sr: [Чо̀век без сло̀боде ка̏о ри̑ба без во̀де].
examples.en: A man without freedom is like a fish out of water.

meanings: what would you like? (a seller's or waiter's question)
here you are (when handing something over)

examples.en: - Can I help you? - One coffee, please.

note: As an answer when handing something over: «Изволите!» - here you are.

examples.sr: [Ја̑ ћу до̀маћу ка̀фу], а за жену капућино.
examples.en: I'll have a Serbian coffee, and a cappuccino for my wife.

note: Direct forms of ordering are polite: «Једну кафу, молим»; «Мени једну домаћу».

key: phr:могу ли добити још једну чашу воде
meanings: could I have another glass of water?
forms: literally: can I get one more glass of water

examples.sr: Извините, [мо̀гу ли до̀бити јо̏ш је̏дну ча̑шу во̀де]?
examples.en: Excuse me, could I have another glass of water?

note: The polite «могу ли» form suits additional requests best.

forms: literally: I'll take that, I ask you

examples.sr: [У̀зе̄ћу то̑], молим вас, и ону мајицу.
examples.en: I'll take this, please, and that T-shirt.

meanings: do you have any discounts or sales?
forms: literally: do you have some discounts

examples.en: Do you have any discounts on jackets?

forms: literally: for here or for carrying

examples.sr: - [За о́вде и̏ли за понѐти]? - За понети.
examples.en: - For here or to go? - To go.

note: Grammatically rough (an infinitive after a preposition), but everyone says it in fast food. Literary: «Хоћете ли јести овде или ћете понети?»

meanings: oh, it's nothing (in reply to thanks or a gift)

examples.sr: Хвала на поклону! - [Ма̏ ка̀квӣ, нѝје то̑ ни̏шта].
examples.en: Thanks for the gift! - Oh, it's nothing.

note: People usually wave a gift away at first: it is politeness.

key: phr:ако не можеш више, једи без хлеба
forms: literally: if you can't any more, eat without bread

examples.sr: Једи још! [А̏ко не мо̏жеш ви̏ше, је̏ди без хле̏ба].
examples.en: Eat some more! If you can't eat any more, eat without bread.

note: How hostesses show love and treat guests to excess.

meanings: so what are you waiting for? (about marriage, kids)
forms: literally: so what are you waiting for

examples.sr: Имате добар посао и стан, [па шта̏ че̏кате]?
examples.en: You have a good job and an apartment, so what are you waiting for?

note: A typical question from relatives to a couple. Another: «Кад ће дете?» - when will the baby come?

forms: literally: again you fixed my day for me

examples.sr: Хвала на поруци: [о̏пе̄т си ми попра̀вио да̑н].
examples.en: Thanks for the message: you've made my day again.

note: To a woman: «поправила».

key: phr:мислим да почињеш да ми се свиђаш
meanings: I think I'm starting to like you
forms: literally: I think you're starting to appeal to me

examples.sr: [Ми̏слӣм да по̀чињеш да ми се сви̏ђаш].
examples.en: I think I'm starting to like you.

note: «Свиђати се» means to be pleasing: the one who likes goes in the dative («ми»).

examples.en: Thanks, I'm full.

note: A woman says «сита сам».

meanings: hey, how's it going? (when you haven't met in a while)

examples.sr: [Де̏ си], бре, одавно те нисам видео!
examples.en: Hey, man, I haven't seen you in ages!

note: Not a question about place; other variants: «Ди си ти?», «Еј, де си».

meanings: to grab a bite on the go
forms: literally: to eat something on one's feet

examples.sr: Журим се, па ћу [по̀јести не̏што с но̑гу].
examples.en: I'm in a hurry, so I'll grab a bite on the go.
Any toppings? - A bit of everything.

note: In Serbian fast food you can take as many toppings as you like at no extra charge.

examples.en: I have to go. Well, bye!

note: «Здраво» and «ћао» mean both 'hi' and 'bye'; «ај» softens it.

forms: literally: may the bugs eat you all night

examples.sr: Лаку ноћ, [је̏ле те бу̀бе це̑лу но̑ћ]!
examples.en: Good night, may the bugs eat you all night long!

note: Only for close friends, as a joke.

examples.en: Come off it! I don't believe you.

note: «Бре» adds emphasis; informal speech only.

key: phr:испуни године животом, а не живот годинама
meanings: fill your years with life, not your life with years (a birthday wish)
forms: literally: fill the years with life, not life with years

examples.sr: Желим ти: [испу̀ни годѝне живо̀том, а не жѝвот го̏динама].
examples.en: I wish you this: fill your years with life, not your life with years.

key: phr:нек' ти срце, новчаник и кревет никад не буду празни
meanings: may your heart, wallet and bed never be empty (a joking wish)
forms: literally: may your heart, wallet and bed never be empty

examples.sr: За рођендан ти желим: [не̏к' ти ср̏це, новча̀нӣк и крѐвет ни̏кад не бу̏ду пра́знӣ].
examples.en: For your birthday I wish you this: may your heart, wallet and bed never be empty.

note: Joking, for friends.

forms: literally: I am your new neighbor

examples.sr: Добар дан! [Ја̑ сам ва̑ш но̀ви ко̀мшија], зовем се Марко.
examples.en: Hello! I'm your new neighbor, my name is Marko.

note: Serbs usually greet their neighbors and ask how they are.

key: phr:да ли бисте могли да припазите на мој стан
meanings: could you keep an eye on my apartment?
forms: literally: would you be able to look after my apartment

examples.sr: Одлазим на пар дана, [да ли бисте мо̏гли да припа̀зите на мо̑ј ста̑н]?
examples.en: I'm leaving for a couple of days, could you keep an eye on my apartment?

meanings: can you take me to...? (in a taxi)
forms: literally: can you drive me to

examples.sr: [Мо̏жете ли ме одвѐсти до] железничке станице?
examples.en: Can you take me to the train station?

meanings: how long will it take to get to...?
forms: literally: how long will the road to... last

examples.en: How long will it take to get to the airport?

note: A cab driver's answer: «Зависи од саобраћаја» (it depends on traffic).

meanings: could you slow down a little?
forms: literally: can you slow down a little

examples.sr: [Мо̏жете ли ма̏ло да успо̀рите], молим вас?
examples.en: Could you slow down a little, please?

meanings: when are you having a baby? (a typical tactless question)
forms: literally: when will the child be

examples.en: Auntie keeps asking: when are you having a baby?

note: If there is already a child: «Кад ће друго?» (when's the second).

key: phr:од смрада још нико није умро, али од упале плућа јесте
meanings: stuffy air never killed anyone, but pneumonia has (the draft argument)
forms: literally: nobody has died of a stink yet, but of pneumonia they have

examples.sr: Баба каже: [од смра̑да јо̏ш ни̏ко нѝје у̏мро, а̏ли од упа̀ле плу́ћа је̏сте].
examples.en: Grandma says: nobody has ever died of stuffy air, but people have died of pneumonia.

note: A typical argument of Serbs against open windows («промаја»).

key: phr:затвори тај прозор, убиће нас промаја
meanings: close that window, the draft will kill us
forms: literally: close that window, the draft will kill us

examples.en: Close that window, the draft will kill us!

note: The classic line against drafts; said both jokingly and in earnest.

examples.en: How are you? - Never better!

note: Other answers: «Одлично сам», «Онако» (so-so), «Нисам никако» (couldn't be worse).

examples.en: I want a beer that's ice cold.

meanings: a wish for wealth and happiness
forms: literally: may God give him white bees

examples.sr: Деда је вредно радио, па му је [Бо̑г да̑о бѐле пчѐле].
examples.en: Grandpa worked hard, so God blessed him with prosperity.

note: In Serbian tradition the white bee stands for prosperity and many descendants. An old blessing.

examples.sr: [Што̏ се ти̑че] посла, све је у реду.
examples.en: As for work, everything is fine.

note: Followed by the genitive: «што се тиче посла». An introductory phrase.

examples.sr: Станови су скупи, а [са дру̑ге стра̑не], комшилук је леп.
examples.en: Apartments are expensive, but on the other hand, the neighborhood is nice.

note: Often paired: «с једне стране ... са друге стране» (on the one hand ... on the other).

meanings: can I pet him? (of a dog)

examples.sr: Какав фин пас! [Мо̀гу ли да га ма̏зим]?
examples.en: What a nice dog! Can I pet him?

note: A common question to a dog's owner on a walk. For a female dog: «Могу ли да је мазим?»

forms: literally: awkward as a short blanket

examples.en: He's impossible to please, like a short blanket.

note: Colloquial; «зајебан» is coarse but not a real swear word. The image: with a short blanket, either your feet or your shoulders freeze.

meanings: that doesn't suit you at all
forms: literally: it fits you like breasts on a chick

examples.sr: Тај сако ти [сто̀јӣ ка̏о пѝлету сѝсе].
examples.en: That jacket looks terrible on you.

note: A colloquial, rather coarse mockery: about unsuitable clothes, and also about someone pretending to be what they are not.

forms: literally: rushed like a pensioner at the counter

examples.sr: Сви су [нава̀лили ка̏о пензио̀нери на ша̀лтер].
examples.en: Everyone rushed forward like pensioners at a counter.

note: A joking comparison: about a crowd pushing in without waiting its turn. One of a series of popular Serbian «као...» comparisons.

meanings: to huff and puff, to groan with tiredness

examples.en: Why are you huffing and puffing like a Yugo going uphill?

note: The Yugo was a small Yugoslav car. A joke about a weak engine on a hill.

examples.en: We drank mulled wine at the market.

note: A popular autumn and winter drink: red wine with spices and sugar.
